key_insight: A 3D CNN can learn subgrid turbulent transport in quiet-Sun simulations and predict Reynolds stress tensor components more accurately than traditional turbulence models.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven surrogate for unresolved solar-plasma turbulence, potentially improving momentum transport and energy dissipation modeling in radiative hydrodynamic simulations.
method: Built a 3D CNN to capture spatial dependencies in velocity fields.
Combined velocity components with scalar plasma features such as density.
Compared against an MLP plus Gradient and Smagorinsky physics-based models, and tested log-transforming skewed stress targets.
evidence_signal: The final 3D CNN improved average prediction by about 31% on diagonal Reynolds-stress components and about 8% on off-diagonal components, with the best performance after log-transforming the targets.
watch_item: Performance is reported for simulated quiet-Sun data, so generalization to other solar conditions or grid resolutions may require additional validation.
paper_title: Developing Machine Learning Models of Subgrid Turbulent Transport for Quiet Sun 3D Radiative Hydrodynamic Simulations
